bull.probability_evidence: Insiders including CEO Anthony Tan bought roughly $30M of stock after shares hit a 3-year low (Reuters 2026-09-23; TipRanks 2026-09-22), short interest fell 18.7% month-on-month (factsheet ST), and five straight years of margin improvement with EV/Sales (2.1x) below its own 5y minimum (3.9x, factsheet RA) support a re-rating case; probability kept at 25% because the mechanical fair-value table's own base/bull figures lean on pre-profit-era multiples (5y max EV/Sales 52.9x) and were discounted by the evaluator down to the fact sheet's bear fair value of 4.43, signalling this path is plausible but not modal.

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Valuation table (RA; peers P:SE,P:UBER,P:HKG:3690): peer-median-implied prices from current price $3.08 scaled by each multiple vs peer median: P/E 26.9x->peer 25.7x implies $2.943; EV/EBITDA 23.2x->peer 19.4x implies $2.576; EV/Sales 2.1x->peer 1.9x implies $2.787 (P/B excluded: note §3 flags peers as more capital-light, not comparable). Half-spread $0.184 / average implied price $2.768 = 6.6%; well under the 33.3% blended residual vol (mc-inputs regression.residual_vol.blended).

base.probability_evidence: EV/Sales (2.1x) sits close to the peer median (1.9x; factsheet RA, peers SE/UBER/HKG:3690) rather than at an extreme, while the stock trades below both its 50-day (3.33) and 200-day (3.80) moving averages (factsheet ST,HI) and carries a weak Piotroski F-score of 2 and Altman Z of 0.61 (factsheet ST) — a muddled quality/valuation picture consistent with a reversion toward the recent 50-day average rather than a re-rating or a further breakdown, which the evaluator weights as the modal (highest-probability) outcome.
